sanskrit: yāṃ tāṃ śriyam asūyāmaḥ purā yātāṃ yudhiṣṭhire adya tām anujānīmo bhīṣmadroṇavadhena ca
english: That sovereign splendour which we once begrudged when it passed long ago to Yudhiṣṭhira—today, with the slaying of Bhīṣma and Droṇa, we acknowledge it as his.

sanskrit: tathā ca matkṛte prāptaḥ kurūṇām eṣa saṃkṣayaḥ pakvānāṃ hi vadhe sūta vajrāyante tṛṇāny api
english: And so, through my doing, this destruction of the Kurus has come to pass; for when the ripe are to be slain, O charioteer, even blades of grass become as thunderbolts.

sanskrit: ananyam idam aiśvaryaṃ loke prāpto yudhiṣṭhiraḥ yasya kopān maheṣvāsau bhīṣmadroṇau nipātitau
english: Yudhiṣṭhira has gained in this world a sovereignty that has no rival—he by whose wrath those two great archers, Bhīṣma and Droṇa, have been struck down.

sanskrit: prāptaḥ prakṛtito dharmo nādharmo mānavān prati krūraḥ sarvavināśāya kālaḥ samativartate
english: By its very nature righteousness has prevailed over men, not unrighteousness; yet cruel Time, bent on the ruin of all, overrides every law.

sanskrit: anyathā cintitā hy arthā narais tāta manasvibhiḥ anyathaiva hi gacchanti daivād iti matir mama
english: For the aims that thoughtful men devise in one way, my son, turn out quite otherwise; this, I hold, is the work of fate.

sanskrit: tasmād aparihārye 'rthe saṃprāpte kṛcchra uttame apāraṇīye duścintye yathābhūtaṃ pracakṣva me
english: Therefore, since a thing unavoidable, a calamity most grievous, beyond crossing and beyond comprehension, has befallen us, tell me how it truly came about.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hanta te varṇayiṣyāmi sarvaṃ pratyakṣadarśivān yathā sa nyapatad droṇaḥ sāditaḥ pāṇḍusṛñjayaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Come then, I shall describe it all to you, for I saw it with my own eyes—how Droṇa fell, brought low by the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas.

sanskrit: senāpatitvaṃ saṃprāpya bhāradvājo mahārathaḥ madhye sarvasya sainyasya putraṃ te vākyam abravīt
english: Having attained the command of the army, Bhāradvāja, that mighty car-warrior, in the midst of all the host spoke these words to your son.

sanskrit: yat kauravāṇām ṛṣabhād āpageyād anantaram senāpatyena māṃ rājann adya satkṛtavān asi
english: "In that next after the bull of the Kurus, the son of the river Gaṅgā, you have today honoured me, O king, with the office of commander,

sanskrit: sadṛśaṃ karmaṇas tasya phalaṃ prāpnuhi pārthiva karomi kāmaṃ kaṃ te 'dya pravṛṇīṣva yam icchasi
english: receive a reward worthy of that deed, O prince. I will grant your wish: choose now whatever boon you desire."

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaś cintya karṇaduḥśāsanādibhiḥ tam athovāca durdharṣam ācāryaṃ jayatāṃ varam
english: Then Duryodhana, having taken counsel with Karṇa, Duḥśāsana, and the rest, spoke thus to the unassailable teacher, the foremost of the victorious:

sanskrit: dadāsi ced varaṃ mahyaṃ jīvagrāhaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram gṛhītvā rathināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ matsamīpam ihānaya
english: "If you grant me a boon, then seize Yudhiṣṭhira alive—take that best of car-warriors captive and bring him here before me."

sanskrit: tataḥ kurūṇām ācāryaḥ śrutvā putrasya te vacaḥ senāṃ praharṣayan sarvām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then the teacher of the Kurus, hearing your son's words, gladdening the whole army, spoke these words:

sanskrit: dhanyaḥ kuntīsuto rājā yasya grahaṇam icchasi na vadhārthaṃ sudurdharṣa varam adya prayācasi
english: "Blessed is King Kuntī's son, whose capture you desire; for it is not his death, O unconquerable one, that you ask of me as a boon today.

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ ca naravyāghra na vadhaṃ tasya kāṅkṣasi nāśaṃsasi kriyām etāṃ matto duryodhana dhruvam
english: And why, O tiger among men, do you not crave his slaying? You surely do not wish this deed of me, Duryodhana.

sanskrit: āho svid dharmaputrasya dveṣṭā tasya na vidyate yad icchasi tvaṃ jīvantaṃ kulaṃ rakṣasi cātmani
english: Or is it that the son of Dharma has no hater anywhere, that you wish him alive and so preserve the lineage within yourself?

sanskrit: atha vā bharataśreṣṭha nirjitya yudhi pāṇḍavān rājyāṃśaṃ pratidattvā ca saubhrātraṃ kartum icchasi
english: Or rather, O best of the Bhāratas, having conquered the Pāṇḍavas in battle and restored to them their share of the kingdom, do you wish to make brotherhood with them?

sanskrit: dhanyaḥ kuntīsuto rājā sujātā cāsya dhīmataḥ ajātaśatrutā satyā tasya yat snihyate bhavān
english: Blessed is King Kuntī's son, and well earned is that wise man's name—Ajātaśatru, 'he whose enemy is not born'—proven true, since even you bear him such affection."

sanskrit: droṇena tv evam uktasya tava putrasya bhārata sahasā niḥsṛto bhāvo yo 'sya nityaṃ pravartate
english: But when Droṇa had spoken thus, O Bhārata, from your son there suddenly broke forth that disposition which forever moves within him.

sanskrit: nākāro gūhituṃ śakyo bṛhaspatisamair api tasmāt tava suto rājan prahṛṣṭo vākyam abravīt
english: A man's true bent cannot be hidden, not even by those equal to Bṛhaspati; and so your son, O king, in his eagerness, spoke these words:

sanskrit: vadhe kuntīsutasyājau nācārya vijayo mama hate yudhiṣṭhire pārtho hanyāt sarvān hi no dhruvam
english: "In the slaying of Kuntī's son in battle, O teacher, lies no victory for me; for were Yudhiṣṭhira killed, the son of Pṛthā would surely slay us all.

sanskrit: na ca śakyo raṇe sarvair nihantum amarair api ya eva caiṣāṃ śeṣaḥ syāt sa evāsmān na śeṣayet
english: Nor can they all be killed in war, not even by the immortals; and whichever of them might be left would leave none of us remaining.

sanskrit: satyapratijñe tv ānīte punardyūtena nirjite punar yāsyanty araṇyāya kaunteyās tam anuvratāḥ
english: But once he whose vows are true is brought here and defeated again at dice, the sons of Kuntī, devoted to him, will go once more into the forest.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ mama jayo vyaktaṃ dīrghakālaṃ bhaviṣyati ato na vadham icchāmi dharmarājasya karhi cit
english: Such, plainly, would be my victory, and it would last a long while. Therefore I do not in any way wish the death of the Dharma-king."

sanskrit: tasya jihmam abhiprāyaṃ jñātvā droṇo 'rthatattvavit taṃ varaṃ sāntaraṃ tasmai dadau saṃcintya buddhimān
english: Knowing his crooked intent, Droṇa, who understood the true nature of things, having reflected, granted him that boon—but with a reservation, wise as he was.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca na ced yudhiṣṭhiraṃ vīra pālayed arjuno yudhi manyasva pāṇḍavaṃ jyeṣṭham ānītaṃ vaśam ātmanaḥ
english: Droṇa said: "If Arjuna does not guard Yudhiṣṭhira in the battle, O hero, then count the eldest Pāṇḍava as already brought into your power.

sanskrit: na hi pārtho raṇe śakyaḥ sendrair devāsurair api pratyudyātum atas tāta naitad āmarṣayāmy aham
english: For the son of Pṛthā cannot be withstood in battle, not even by the gods and demons together with Indra; and so, my son, I will not provoke that contest.

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ sa śiṣyo me matpūrvaś cāstrakarmaṇi taruṇaḥ kīrtiyuktaś ca ekāyanagataś ca saḥ
english: Beyond doubt he is my pupil, and in the wielding of weapons he had me first as his teacher; yet he is young, crowned with fame, and wholly single-minded in his course.

sanskrit: astrāṇīndrāc ca rudrāc ca bhūyāṃsi samavāptavān amarṣitaś ca te rājaṃs tena nāmarṣayāmy aham
english: He has gained many weapons from Indra and from Rudra, and he is full of indignation against you, O king; for that reason I will not rouse him.

sanskrit: sa cāpakramyatāṃ yuddhād yenopāyena śakyate apanīte tataḥ pārthe dharmarājo jitas tvayā
english: Let him be drawn away from the battle by whatever means is possible; and once the son of Pṛthā is removed, the Dharma-king is as good as conquered by you.

sanskrit: grahaṇaṃ cej jayaṃ tasya manyase puruṣarṣabha etena cābhyupāyena dhruvaṃ grahaṇam eṣyati
english: If you reckon his capture to be victory, O bull among men, then by this expedient his capture will surely come to pass.

sanskrit: ahaṃ gṛhītvā rājānaṃ satyadharmaparāyaṇam ānayiṣyāmi te rājan vaśam adya na saṃśayaḥ
english: I will seize the king, devoted to truth and righteousness, and bring him into your power this very day, O king—of that there is no doubt,

sanskrit: yadi sthāsyati saṃgrāme muhūrtam api me 'grataḥ apanīte naravyāghre kuntīputre dhanaṃjaye
english: if only he will stand before me in the fray for even a moment, once that tiger among men, Kuntī's son Dhanaṃjaya, has been led away.

sanskrit: phalgunasya samakṣaṃ tu na hi pārtho yudhiṣṭhiraḥ grahītuṃ samare śakyaḥ sendrair api surāsuraiḥ
english: But in Phalguna's very presence, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Pṛthā cannot be taken in battle, not even by the gods and demons together with Indra."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sāntaraṃ tu pratijñāte rājño droṇena nigrahe gṛhītaṃ tam amanyanta tava putrāḥ subāliśāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: But when Droṇa had pledged the king's capture with that reservation, your sons, foolish as they were, deemed him already taken.

sanskrit: pāṇḍaveṣu hi sāpekṣaṃ droṇaṃ jānāti te sutaḥ tataḥ pratijñāsthairyārthaṃ sa mantro bahulīkṛtaḥ
english: Your son knew that Droṇa was partial toward the Pāṇḍavas; and therefore, to make the pledge seem firm, that counsel was spread far and wide.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanenāpi grahaṇaṃ pāṇḍavasya tat sainyasthāneṣu sarveṣu vyāghoṣitam ariṃdama
english: Then by Duryodhana too that capture of the Pāṇḍava was proclaimed aloud throughout all the stations of the army, O crusher of foes.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tatas te sainikāḥ śrutvā taṃ yudhiṣṭhiranigraham siṃhanādaravāṃś cakrur bāṇaśaṅkharavaiḥ saha
english: Saṃjaya said: Then those soldiers, hearing of that capture of Yudhiṣṭhira, raised lion-roars together with the clamour of arrows and conch-shells.

sanskrit: tat tu sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ dharmarājena bhārata āptair āśu parijñātaṃ bhāradvājacikīrṣitam
english: But all that had taken place—Bhāradvāja's design—was swiftly learned in full by the Dharma-king, O Bhārata, through trusted men.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvān samānāyya bhrātṝn sainyāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ abravīd dharmarājas tu dhanaṃjayam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then, having summoned all his brothers and the troops on every side, the Dharma-king spoke these words to Dhanaṃjaya:

sanskrit: śrutaṃ te puruṣavyāghra droṇasyādya cikīrṣitam yathā tan na bhavet satyaṃ tathā nītir vidhīyatām
english: "You have heard, O tiger among men, what Droṇa intends to do today; let such a course be devised that it may not come true.

sanskrit: sāntaraṃ hi pratijñātaṃ droṇenāmitrakarśana tac cāntaram amogheṣau tvayi tena samāhitam
english: For Droṇa has made his pledge with a reservation, O scourge of foes, and that reservation he has fixed upon you, whose every arrow strikes home.

sanskrit: sa tvam adya mahābāho yudhyasva madanantaram yathā duryodhanaḥ kāmaṃ nemaṃ droṇād avāpnuyāt
english: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, fight today close at my side, so that Duryodhana may not gain this wish from Droṇa."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca yathā me na vadhaḥ kārya ācāryasya kathaṃ cana tathā tava parityāgo na me rājaṃś cikīrṣitaḥ
english: Arjuna said: "As the slaying of the teacher is by no means a thing I would do, so neither, O king, is your abandonment anything I would intend.

sanskrit: apy evaṃ pāṇḍava prāṇān utsṛjeyam ahaṃ yudhi pratīyāṃ nāham ācāryaṃ tvāṃ na jahyāṃ kathaṃ cana
english: Even so, O Pāṇḍava, I would sooner give up my life in battle—I will not turn against the teacher, nor will I ever forsake you in any way.

sanskrit: tvāṃ nigṛhyāhave rājan dhārtarāṣṭro yam icchati na sa taṃ jīvaloke 'smin kāmaṃ prāptaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: That wish which Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son cherishes—to seize you in battle, O king—he shall in no way attain so long as I live in this world of the living.

sanskrit: prapated dyauḥ sanakṣatrā pṛthivī śakalībhavet na tvāṃ droṇo nigṛhṇīyāj jīvamāne mayi dhruvam
english: Sooner might the sky fall with its stars, sooner might the earth break into fragments, than Droṇa take you captive while I yet live—of this be certain.

sanskrit: yadi tasya raṇe sāhyaṃ kurute vajrabhṛt svayam devair vā sahito daityair na tvāṃ prāpsyaty asau mṛdhe
english: Even if the wielder of the thunderbolt himself should aid him in the fight, or the gods together with the demons, he shall not reach you in the battle.

sanskrit: mayi jīvati rājendra na bhayaṃ kartum arhasi droṇād astrabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhāt sarvaśastrabhṛtām api
english: While I live, O lord of kings, you ought to feel no fear of Droṇa, foremost of all who bear weapons, nor of any other wielder of arms.

sanskrit: na smarāmy anṛtāṃ vācaṃ na smarāmi parājayam na smarāmi pratiśrutya kiṃ cid apy anapākṛtam
english: I do not recall an untrue word from my lips, I do not recall a defeat, nor do I recall ever having promised a thing and left it undone."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca mṛdaṅgāś cānakaiḥ saha prāvādyanta mahārāja pāṇḍavānāṃ niveśane
english: Saṃjaya said: Then conches and kettledrums and tabors, together with war-drums, sounded out, O great king, in the encampment of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: siṃhanādaś ca saṃjajñe pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām dhanurjyātalaśabdaś ca gaganaspṛk subhairavaḥ
english: And a lion-roar arose from the great-souled Pāṇḍavas, and the sound of bowstrings slapped from the palm, touching the heavens, most terrible.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā śaṅkhanirghoṣaṃ pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ tvadīyeṣv apy anīkeṣu vāditrāṇy abhijaghnire
english: Hearing that blare of the conch of the great-souled Pāṇḍava, in your own ranks too the instruments were struck up in answer.

sanskrit: tato vyūḍhāny anīkāni tava teṣāṃ ca bhārata śanair upeyur anyonyaṃ yotsyamānāni saṃyuge
english: Then the marshalled hosts, both yours and theirs, O Bhārata, advanced slowly toward one another, ready to do battle in the field.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca droṇapāñcālyayor api
english: Then there broke out a tumultuous, hair-raising battle between the Pāṇḍavas and the Kurus, and between Droṇa and the Pāñcāla prince.

sanskrit: yatamānāḥ prayatnena droṇānīkaviśātane na śekuḥ sṛñjayā rājaṃs tad dhi droṇena pālitam
english: Striving with all their effort to shatter Droṇa's array, the Sṛñjayas could not prevail, O king, for it was guarded by Droṇa himself.

sanskrit: tathaiva tava putrasya rathodārāḥ prahāriṇaḥ na śekuḥ pāṇḍavīṃ senāṃ pālyamānāṃ kirīṭinā
english: Likewise the noble, hard-striking car-warriors of your son could not break the Pāṇḍava army, guarded as it was by the Diademed One.

sanskrit: āstāṃ te stimite sene rakṣyamāṇe parasparam saṃprasupte yathā naktaṃ vanarājyau supuṣpite
english: Both those armies stood motionless, each warding off the other, like two fair-flowering forest-tracts asleep together in the night.

sanskrit: tato rukmaratho rājann arkeṇeva virājatā varūthinā viniṣpatya vyacarat pṛtanāntare
english: Then the warrior of the golden car, O king, blazing like the very sun with his guard-railed chariot, dashed forth and ranged through the midst of the host.

sanskrit: tam udyataṃ rathenaikam āśukāriṇam āhave anekam iva saṃtrāsān menire pāṇḍusṛñjayāḥ
english: Him, raised aloft and alone upon his chariot, swift in action in the fray, the Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas in their terror reckoned to be many.

sanskrit: tena muktāḥ śarā ghorā viceruḥ sarvatodiśam trāsayanto mahārāja pāṇḍaveyasya vāhinīm
english: The dreadful arrows loosed by him ranged in every direction, terrifying, O great king, the army of the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: madhyaṃ dinam anuprāpto gabhastiśatasaṃvṛtaḥ yathādṛśyata gharmāṃśus tathā droṇo 'py adṛśyata
english: As the noonday sun, ringed about with its hundred rays, appears when it reaches the meridian, so too did Droṇa appear.

sanskrit: na cainaṃ pāṇḍaveyānāṃ kaś cic chaknoti māriṣa vīkṣituṃ samare kruddhaṃ mahendram iva dānavāḥ
english: And no one among the Pāṇḍavas, good sir, could so much as look upon him in his battle-fury, as the demons could not gaze upon great Indra.

sanskrit: mohayitvā tataḥ sainyaṃ bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān dhṛṣṭadyumnabalaṃ tūrṇaṃ vyadhaman niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Bhāradvāja, the majestic one, having bewildered the army, swiftly scattered Dhṛṣṭadyumna's force with his whetted arrows.

sanskrit: sa diśaḥ sarvato ruddhvā saṃvṛtya kham ajihmagaiḥ pārṣato yatra tatraiva mamṛde pāṇḍuvāhinīm
english: Blocking the quarters on every side and covering the very sky with his straight-flying shafts, wherever the son of Pṛṣata was, there did he crush the Pāṇḍava host.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ sa pāṇḍavānīke janayaṃs tumulaṃ mahat vyacarat pāṇḍavān droṇo dahan kakṣam ivānalaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, raising a great tumult in the Pāṇḍava ranks, Droṇa ranged among the Pāṇḍavas, burning them as a fire burns dry brushwood.

sanskrit: nirdahantam anīkāni sākṣād agnim ivotthitam dṛṣṭvā rukmarathaṃ yuddhe samakampanta sṛñjayāḥ
english: Seeing the warrior of the golden car consuming their armies, like fire itself risen up in the battle, the Sṛñjayas trembled.

sanskrit: pratataṃ cāsyamānasya dhanuṣo 'syāśukāriṇaḥ jyāghoṣaḥ śrūyate 'tyarthaṃ visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ
english: And as his bow was drawn without pause, swift-dealing, the twang of its string was heard exceedingly loud, like the crash of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: rathinaḥ sādinaś caiva nāgān aśvān padātinaḥ raudrā hastavatā muktāḥ pramathnanti sma sāyakāḥ
english: Car-warriors and horsemen, elephants, steeds, and foot-soldiers—the fierce shafts loosed by that deft-handed one ground them all to ruin.

sanskrit: nānadyamānaḥ parjanyaḥ sānilaḥ śucisaṃkṣaye aśmavarṣam ivāvarṣat pareṣām āvahad bhayam
english: Like a thundering rain-cloud, wind-driven at summer's end, raining down a hail of stones, he poured forth terror upon his foes.

sanskrit: vyacarat sa tadā rājan senāṃ vikṣobhayan prabhuḥ vardhayām āsa saṃtrāsaṃ śātravāṇām amānuṣam
english: Then that lord ranged on, O king, throwing the host into turmoil, and swelled in his enemies a terror more than human.

sanskrit: tasya vidyud ivābhreṣu cāpaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam bhramad rathāmbude tasmin dṛśyate sma punaḥ punaḥ
english: His bow, adorned with gold, sweeping about upon that chariot-cloud, was seen again and again like lightning amid the storm-clouds.

sanskrit: sa vīraḥ satyavān prājño dharmanityaḥ sudāruṇaḥ yugāntakāle yanteva raudrāṃ prāskandayan nadīm
english: That hero, truthful, wise, ever devoted to righteousness, yet now most terrible, set surging a dreadful river, like the driver of doom at the ending of an age—

sanskrit: amarṣavegaprabhavāṃ kravyādagaṇasaṃkulām balaughaiḥ sarvataḥ pūrṇāṃ vīravṛkṣāpahāriṇīm
english: a river born of the rushing torrent of his wrath, thronged with flocks of flesh-eating beasts, brimming on every side with floods of soldiery, sweeping away heroes as its trees;

sanskrit: śoṇitodāṃ rathāvartāṃ hastyaśvakṛtarodhasam kavacoḍupasaṃyuktāṃ māṃsapaṅkasamākulām
english: its water blood, its whirlpools chariots, its banks built of elephants and horses, carrying coats of mail as its rafts, choked with the mire of flesh;

sanskrit: medomajjāsthisikatām uṣṇīṣavaraphenilām saṃgrāmajaladāpūrṇāṃ prāsamatsyasamākulām
english: its sands fat and marrow and bone, foaming with fine turbans, filled by the rain-clouds of war, teeming with javelins for fish;

sanskrit: naranāgāśvasaṃbhūtāṃ śaravegaughavāhinīm śarīradāruśṛṅgāṭāṃ bhujanāgasamākulām
english: sprung from men and elephants and horses, bearing along its swift flood of arrows, with corpses for its driftwood and water-chestnuts, swarming with arms for its water-snakes;

sanskrit: uttamāṅgopalatalāṃ nistriṃśajhaṣasevitām rathanāgahradopetāṃ nānābharaṇanīrajām
english: its pebbled bed strewn with severed heads, haunted by swords for sharks, set with deep pools of chariots and elephants, its lotuses the manifold ornaments;

sanskrit: mahārathaśatāvartāṃ bhūmireṇūrmimālinīm mahāvīryavatāṃ saṃkhye sutarāṃ bhīrudustarām
english: with eddies of hundreds of great car-warriors, garlanded with waves of the dust of the earth—easy to cross for the mighty in battle, but for the timid impassable;

sanskrit: śūravyālasamākīrṇāṃ prāṇivāṇijasevitām chinnacchatramahāhaṃsāṃ mukuṭāṇḍajasaṃkulām
english: strewn with heroes for its serpents, frequented by living men for its traders, its great swans the severed parasols, thronged with diadems for its water-birds.
